name: Deinos Herd
body:
Deinos Herd
CR 7

A hungry light glows in the eyes of this otherwise normal-looking horse. It neighs at you threateningly, while baring teeth more pointed than usual.

XP 3,200
NE Large magical beast (troop)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 17, flat-footed 11 (+6 Dex, +1 dodge, +3 natural, -1 size)
hp 85 (10d8+40)
Fort +11, Ref +13, Will +8
Defensive Abilities troop traits

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee troop (2d6+6)
Space 30 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks blood rage, screaming whinny, trample (2d6+9, DC 21)

STATISTICS

Str 22, Dex 22, Con 18, Int 7, Wis 17, Cha 11
Base Atk +6; CMB +13; CMD 30 (34 vs. trip)
Feats Dodge, Endurance, Improved Natural Armor, Intimidating Prowess, Iron Will, Runb
Skills Intimidate +11, Perception +11
Languages Abyssal, Common, Infernal (cannot speak)

ECOLOGY

Screaming Whinny (Ex)

A deinos herd can make an Intimidate check to demoralize one creature it threatens as a swift action, or a single Intimidate check against all creatures it threatens as a full-round action.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate plains
Organization solitary or horde (2-10)
Treasure none

These sinister stallions and magnificent mares are related to ordinary horses and at first glance they are simply strong and sleek horses, well-muscled and with shining coats but otherwise unremarkable. At times, they even behave like ordinary horses, if spirited and headstrong. However, they carry a hidden and accursed nature, an uncanny taste for flesh and blood, especially for humanoids. While no more intelligent than other animals, they cunning enough to be capable of subterfuge, feigning docility in order to draw close to their prey. When inflamed with bloodlust, however, they are tireless in pursuit of their prey, inspiring terror with their screaming whinnies.

Legend tells that the first deinos were bred from ordinary horses by a cruel king, who fed his royal herd on the flesh of unsuspecting guests or strangers to his island. He kept them lashed with iron chains to their feasting troughs, releasing them from time to time to terrorize the countryside until a mighty hero overcame them and lashed them to his own chariot, feeding the cruel king to his own mares before binding their mouths and calming their spirits for a time.

Many horses sired or foaled from that lineage grow up as ordinary horses, though of excellent stock, but in others the madness of their sires and dams breeds true and they grow into savage hunters, fleeing into the wild.
